title: How Dagobert Renouf grew from 150 to 15k Twitter followers and bootstrapped Logology
summary: Dagobert Renouf explains how he turned Twitter into Logology's main marketing channel by connecting one-on-one and sharing his founder story. He also covers bootstrapping for freedom, automating his wife's design process into a product, and waiting to launch on Product Hunt until there is momentum.

principles.text: On Twitter, connect one-on-one with people instead of broadcasting like a TED talk.
principles.quote: if you're just like a normal guy or like a startup founder it's all about connecting one-on-one with people so going to people's profile looking at what they do

principles.text: Share your own startup story daily; founders who relate to it are your target customers and become buyers.
principles.quote: basically it's all about sharing my experience and what what happens is other startup founders relate to it and because good news is startup founders well they're my target customers

principles.text: Only plug your product when it is relevant and adds value to the conversation; otherwise it is spam.
principles.quote: the difference is is it relevant is it done with like kind of uh humility like and do you are you trying to be nice and to bring value and or are you just trying to plug your product

principles.text: Skip big VC-oriented startup books when you are tiny and unfunded; experiment yourself and focus on marketing.
principles.quote: i would advise people to not read too much into the big startup books because it doesn't necessarily apply to you if you're tiny and it's a trap because it can make you overthink everything

principles.text: Launch on Product Hunt only once you have a solid product, happy customers and an audience to create momentum.
principles.quote: you wait until you have a pretty solid product happy customers you build some kind of audience around it and that way when you launch you have all that momentum with you

principles.text: Productize an expert's craft by pre-building vetted options and automating the matching, delivering expert quality cheaply.
principles.quote: it's really like we made her into kind of like an automated system okay behind the scenes it's her who worked tirelessly to create all the possibilities
